thesis: IHH has real underlying hospital growth, but the bear carries the premium shareholder-conversion objection. RM141m cash after the specified financing and leases does not cover RM486m owner dividends, with RM11.564bn net debt before leases at 30.38x trailing earnings. Underlying EBITDA and profit growth preserve upside, but financial repair or payout discipline is still prospective, making neutral more defensible than treating expansion as already owner-funded.
strongest_counterexample: Underlying revenue and EBITDA grew 7% and 14%, H1 ex-exceptional profit rose 22%, and RM771m pre-financing FCF demonstrates genuine operating cash before the conservative financing deductions.
invalidation_conditions: Comparable H1 cash after the same investment/finance/lease deductions at least equal to owner dividends, with net debt no higher than RM11.564bn, would defeat the current conversion-restraint thesis.
Comparable H1 ex-exceptional profit below RM1.028bn would undermine the growth counterweight.
decisive_factors: Observed dividend-cash shortfall and leases are material at the premium valuation.
MFRS129-adjusted growth supports operating quality; unresolved governance statements do not justify invented legal outcomes.
